thread:
marie (PM): Hi team — sharing the draft PRD + RFC for the quantized-kernel migration and the KV-cache semantics change. Link: https://rwd/internal/rfcs/quant-kernel-mig. TL;DR: reduce cost by ~30% on common seq lengths, keep correctness parity, and avoid increased OOM risk. Need agreement on launch gates and acceptance criteria by EOD Friday.

 daniel (eng-runtime): skimmed. two quick asks: 1) can we get a perf profile by model size (7B/13B/70B)? 2) what's the expected change to cache hit behavior when quantization changes layout?

 ravi (ml): perf matrix is in the RFC appendix. expected token throughput: +20-35% depending on kernel and batch. cache hit semantics: no change at logical level — but physical KV serialization format will change, so we need a migration path or on-the-fly upgrade.

 kevin (infra): on-the-fly upgrade worries me for live Dedicated pools. If we change serialization, some nodes will have old-format entries. We need a compatibility shim or a tombstone-and-rewrite background job.

 daniel (eng-runtime): agree. propose two options in RFC: (A) compat shim that reads both formats (adds decode cost), (B) drain-and-warm: mark pool draining, migrate KV for active prefixes, then flip. We should choose based on customer tier and SLA.

 sara (sre): rollout gates must include P95 tail latency and OOM rate. Also add auto-rollback if error-rate delta > 0.5% or P95 worsens by >10% for 10m. Add observability hooks to detect KV deserialization errors.

 jen (product): customers ask for explicit opt-in for Dedicated. For hosted API let's do a staged rollout (canary per region) and notify affected customers. Add a product acceptance criterion: no visible quality regressions on our core prompt-set evals.

 marie (PM): putting suggested acceptance criteria here so we can iterate: 1) correctness parity: token-level BLEU/EM on eval set within 0.5% of baseline; 2) perf gains: >=15% median throughput for 13B on common seqs; 3) memory safety: no increase in OOM incidents in canary; 4) stability: no increase in 5xx errors; 5) rollout safety: rollback triggers defined and tested. Please add missing items.

 daniel (eng-runtime): add: stress test for repeated cache evictions and prefix-swap scenarios. Edge case: very long conversation where KV size grows and quant-decode overhead may trigger CPU bottleneck — include CPU consumption in canary metrics.

 ravi (ml): note on model variants: for quantized kernels we plan two variants: Q8 + residual-fix and Q4hf for faster throughput. RFC includes per-variant acceptance windows. We must ensure routing policies map fallback paths to full-precision model variants when quality triggers fire.

 kevin (infra): for Dedicated we need a migration playbook with commands. Example snippet for safe-drain:

```
# drain node
api patch /pools/<id> -p '{"drain": true}'
# kick warm job
job create migrate-kv --pool <id>
```

Also add a k8s OOM budget check before flip.

 sara (sre): CI/Canary tests: automated scenario runner that hits long convo patterns, prefix reuse, and cold-starts. Must run for 4h in alpha, 24h in beta. Instrument KV error histograms and CPU per-token.

 marie (PM): outstanding decisions: (1) choose compat strategy (shim vs drain) per deployment type, (2) canary sizes and durations, (3) fallback routing thresholds. Propose we decide Monday in planning sync. Assign owners: daniel = eng lead, kevin = infra lead, ravi = model lead, sara = SRE lead. I'll own product comms.

 daniel (eng-runtime): noted. I'll add a small patch to RFC with the drain playbook and the shim proposal cost model. Also adding a dev-only decoder flag to allow toggling formats.

 jen (product): also add customer opt-out flow and billing note if cost changes. We should draft an email template for early access customers.

 ci-bot: test-run started for canary pool rp-quant-01. Duration: 6h. Results will post to the PR when finished.

 ravi (ml): edge-case: model hot-start with cache warming where half the prefixes are in old format and half new — we need to ensure merge logic doesn't corrupt token offsets. Add small unit test in runtime to simulate mixed-format KV iter.

 kevin (infra): question for daniel: how heavy is the decode penalty for compat shim? if it's >5% latency on p50 we may prefer drain for latency-critical tenants.

 daniel (eng-runtime): decode adds ~2-6% CPU depending on seq-length distribution — detailed numbers in appendix table. I'll call out thresholds in RFC.

 marie (PM): action items recap: daniel update RFC with drain+shim cost table; kevin draft migration commands and OOM checks; ravi add unit/regression tests for mixed-format KV; sara define canary metric thresholds and rollback automation; jen draft customer comms. Back to me by Monday COB. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

 jen (product): acked. I'll also schedule a 30m sync after RFC update to align comms and opt-in UX.

 sara (sre): adding brief note — ensure logs emit a structured field kv_format_version for easier pivoting in observability.

 daniel (eng-runtime): will do. Also adding a troubleshooting checklist for the playbook: "if decode errors >0.1% then auto-rollback".

 marie (PM): cool. We'll collect final sign-offs in the Monday sync. If anyone has further blockers post-update, drop them here.

 kevin (infra): one more: runbook for unexpected spike in network IO during migration (KV rewrite can be heavy) — add to infra docs.

 marie (PM): noted, adding to infra runbook section of RFC. Closing for now.
